review_notes:
I read the whole file (lines 1–185). It has three public iff lemmas: `ProfiniteGrp.mono_iff_injective`, `ProfiniteGrp.epi_iff_surjective` and `ProfiniteAddGrp.mono_iff_injective`. It also has one private helper and a `to_additive existing` attribute line. The file declares no simp lemmas and no simp-set interactions. Its only simp calls are local ones (`simp only [Function.Surjective, not_forall, not_exists]` and `simp [div_eq_mul_inv]`).

I checked how comparable Mathlib lemmas are set up. The `mono_iff_injective` and `epi_iff_surjective` lemmas for `GrpCat`, `ModuleCat`, `TopCat`, `Profinite`, `CompHaus` and `CompHausLike` carry no `@[simp]` attribute. Adding `@[simp]` here would be a new convention rather than a missing canonical rule. It would also risk unwanted rewriting of `Mono`/`Epi` hypotheses and goals. Downstream uses in `Procyclic.lean` and elsewhere in the repository use these lemmas by explicit `rw` or `.mp`/`.2`, so a simp attribute would not improve them.

The `to_additive existing` line pairs the multiplicative mono lemma with the additive one. `epi_iff_surjective` has no additive counterpart. That is a completeness gap, not a simp-interface problem, so I did not report it. I found no loop, competing-rule or orientation problem. I did not run Lean, so this is a source-reading judgment.
